newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner still looking to sell Cunard.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner still looking to sell Cunard.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian company Kvaerner ASA said on Friday it remained intent on divesting or finding partners for its Cunard cruise line.
In the weekly Tradewinds shipping journal, Paris Katsoufis, Cunard's new president and chief operating officer, claimed that Kvaerner had dropped plans to sell off the subsidiary.
Kvaerner acquired the luxury cruise ship operator last year as part of its takeover of British conglomerate Trafalger House Plc.
Soon after the merger, the construction and engineering specialist said it intended to divest non-core activities, including Cunard.
"Kvaerner's position on Cunard had not changed at all," Paul Emberley, Kvaerner's chief spokesman, told Reuters.

"It is still our intention to pursue the reorganisation of Cunard and to get the business back on to a sustainable profit level. In the medium term we do not expect to be the sole shareholders in Cunard," he said.
